Cœna, ad exemplum Tertulliani, stabilivit, sed verò prætereà hanc corporis Christi præsentiam, quin & participationem, merè Spiritualem urget esse; de priori, ita adversus Marcionitas arguens: Quod si Christus (ut obloquuntur Marcionitæ) carne destitutus erat & exsanguis, cujusmodi Carnis, cujus corporis, qualis tandem sanguinis signa & IMAGINES PANEM ET POCULUM MINISTRAVIT. Dialog. 3. de Homine Christo.
english: Next, Origen (same century): with Tertullian he stabilizes the impropriety of ‘This is my body’ and real presence — then urges that presence and participation are merely Spiritual.
Against Marcionites: if Christ had no flesh and blood, of what flesh and blood did He minister bread and cup as signs and IMAGES?

source_text: De posteriori autem Homil. 7. in Leviticum hacce commentatus: Agnoscite, quia figura sunt, & ideo tanquam spirituales, non carnales, examinate & intelligite, quæ dicuntur; si quasi Carnales accipitis, lædunt vos & non alunt! Est enim in Evangelio Litera, quæ occidit eum, qui non spiritualiter, quæ dicit, ea advertit. SI ENIM SECUNDUM LITERAM SEQUERIS, HOC IPSUM QUOD DICTUM EST: NISI MANDUCAVERITIS CARNEM MEAM ET BIBERITIS SANGUINEM MEUM, OCCIDIT HÆC LITERA.
english: Origen Hom. Lev. 7: recognize they are figures — examine them as spiritual, not carnal; taken carnally they hurt and do not nourish.
The Gospel letter kills whoever does not hear spiritually: if you follow ‘Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood’ according to the letter, that letter kills.

source_text: Tertius denique & jam altius seculum hoc ingressus, divus CYPRIANUS, veram illam ac spiritualem corporis Christi in Eucharistia præsentiam atque participationem, disertissimè omnium, rhetoricô interim stylô (hôc potissimum tempore à Patribus excoli cœptô, facilè autem in abusum trahendo, in sermone de Lapsis populari, Rhetoricæ per se suamque naturam, indulgere solito) inter alia hunc in modum edisserit, dum nempe in eos invehitur, qui ab negatâ semel fide christiana, paulò post leniori pænitentiâ tacti, sicque minus præparati, ad S. cœnam accedunt: Mortiferos, ait, idolorum cibos adhuc penè ructantes, exhalantibus etiamnum scelus suum faucibus & contagia funesta redolentibus, Domini Corpus invadunt. Et iterum. Spretis his omnibus atque contemtis, vis infertur Corpori Christi & sanguini ejus; plus modò in Dominum manibus atque ore delinquunt, quàm cùm Dominum negaverunt. Hinc namque corpus Christi invadere, & huic, nec non Sanguini ejus, vim inferre aliter, quàm Spirituali modô, haud poterant, sumentes nempe Panem & Vinum, seu Sacramentum Domini, ab impiis non nisi per Sacrilegium, usurpandum & attrectandum.
english: Cyprian, later in the century, most expressly teaches true spiritual presence and participation — in rhetorical style (On the Lapsed) against the unprepared who still reek of idol foods yet invade the Lord’s Body.
They can invade Christ’s body and do violence to His blood only in a Spiritual mode — by taking bread and wine, which the impious handle only by sacrilege.
Stop before §.VIII (fourth century: Nicene Fathers).

source_text: §. VIII. Ad QUARTI SECULI Testimonia excutienda pedem promoturus, non possum non meminisse primo omnium locô præstantissimi hujusmodi Testimoniorum complexûs, PATRUM NICÆNORUM verbis concepti, totiusque Ecclesiæ ejus temporis christianæ de S. cœna sententiam aperientis; tantóque magis meminisse, quantò certiùs Formulæ administrandi Cœnam S., in Ecclesiis nostris Reformatis Marchicis aliisque receptæ, verba, administrationem ipsam immediatè antecedentia, complexui isti accepta ferenda videntur, quibus nempe Communicantes admonentur, cogitationibus suis non usque adeò Symbolis Sacris, in S. Cœna sensibus evidentissimè expositis, inhærere, sed verò oculos mentis in Cœlum dirigere, certòque certiùs, quin fide divina, statuere atque tenere, animas suas non minus ipso corpore sanguineque Christi veris ac substantialibus, saginari, quàm Symbola S. ore corporis à se assumantur ac percipiantur.
english: §.VIII: stepping into the FOURTH century, first remember the Nicene Fathers’ complexus — opening the whole Church’s sentence on the Sacred Supper.

Our Marchic Reformed administration formula seems drawn from it: communicants must not cling to the sensed symbols, but lift the mind’s eyes to heaven and by divine faith hold that souls are fed by Christ’s true substantial body and blood no less than the mouth takes the symbols.

source_text: Sic enim verba Nicænorum habent: Ne, inquiunt, proposito pani & poculo humiliter intenti simus, sed sublatâ in altum mente per fidem consideremus, proponi in S. illa Mensa Agnum Dei tollentem peccata mundi, & pretiosum ejus corpus & Sanguinem verè accipientes, nos credamus, hæc esse nostræ Resurrectionis (puta ad vitam æternam) symbola: Nam ideo etiam non multum, sed parum accipimus, ut agnoscamus, quod non ad satietatem, sed ad sanctificationem, accipiamus. Vid. Acta à Gelasio Cyziceno conscripta & ab Abrahamo Sculteto edita, Concilii vestigiis hisce exactissime insistit Catholicorum Patrum ac Theologorum Orthodoxorum omnium facilè princeps S. ATHANASIUS.
english: Nicene words (Gelasius of Cyzicus / Scultetus): do not stay humble-eyed on the set bread and cup — by faith see the Lamb of God on that Table, truly receiving His precious body and Blood as symbols of our resurrection unto eternal life.
We take little, not much — not for satiety but for sanctification. Athanasius most exactly follows these Council footprints.

source_text: Utpote adstruendis Spiritualibus præsentiâ ac participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna, exclusis præsentia & participatione corporalibus, Commentario ad sextum Joh. caput, totus occupatus: Dominus, inquit, Spiritum à carne discriminavit, ut discerneremus ea, quæ loqueretur, non carnalia esse, sed spiritualia: Quod enim hominibus corpus ejus suffecisset ad cibum, ut universi mundi alimonia fieret? Sed proptereà adscensionis suæ in cælum mentionem fecit, ut eos à corporali intellectu abstraheret ac deinde carnem suam, de qua locutus erat, cibum è supernis cælestem & spiritualem alimoniam (pneumatikēn trophēn) ab ipso donandam intelligerent.
english: Athanasius (on John 6) builds spiritual presence and participation of body and blood in the Supper — corporal presence and participation shut out.
The Lord separated Spirit from flesh so we know His speech is spiritual not carnal; He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect toward heavenly spiritual food (pneumatikēn trophēn).

source_text: Quæ enim, inquit, locutus sum vobis, Spiritus & vita sunt, quod perinde est ac si diceret corpus meum, quod ostenditur ac datur pro mundo, in cibum dabitur, ut spiritualiter (pneumatikōs) unicuique tribuatur & fiat singulis præservatio ad resurrectionem vitæ æternæ.
english: ‘What I have spoken to you are Spirit and life’ — as if to say: my body shown and given for the world will be given as food so it is distributed to each spiritually (pneumatikōs).
It becomes for each a preservation unto the resurrection of eternal life.

source_text: Athanasio adstipulatur Rhetorum Sacrorum, circa exitum ejus Seculi, disertissimus, videl. S. AMBROSIUS, mutationem omnem quæ in symbola S. Cœnæ, per consecrationem eorum, competit, nonnisi spiritualem esse indigitans, Lib. 4. de Sacram. cap. 4. Tu ipse, inquit, eras, sed Vetus Creatura, postquam consecratus es, nova creatura esse cœpisti. Et iterum: Tu fortè dices, panis meus usitatus est; sed panis iste panis est, ante verba benedictionis sacramentorum, ubi accesserit consecratio, de pane fit corpus Christi.
english: Ambrose (De Sacr. 4.4), late in the century, agrees: every change that consecration works in the Supper’s symbols is only spiritual.
You yourself were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one. Ordinary bread before the blessing-words; when consecration comes, from bread is made Christ’s body.

source_text: Hoc igitur adstruemus, quomodo qui panis est, potest esse corpus Christi consecratione. Consecratio autem fit verbis Domini, ut venerabile Sacramentum conficiatur. Vides quàm operatorius sit sermo Christi. Si ergo tanta vis est in sermone Domini, ut inciperent esse, (panis & vinum) quæ non erant, & in aliud commutentur, Ergo, ut Tibi respondeam, non erat corpus Christi ante consecrationem, sed post consecrationem jam est corpus Christi. Ipse dixit & factum est; TU IPSE ERAS, SED ERAS VETUS CREATURA; POSTQUAM CONSECRATUS ES, NOVA CREATURA ESSE CŒPISTI.
english: How can what is bread be Christ’s body by consecration? By the Lord’s words the sacrament is made — Christ’s speech is operative.

If bread and wine begin to be what they were not and are changed into another, then it was not Christ’s body before consecration, but after it is. He spoke and it was done: you were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one.
Stop before §.IX (fifth century: Chrysostom and Augustine).

source_text: §. IX. Testimonia SECULI QUINTI, seu postremi eorum, quibus de puriori doctrina Evangelica gloriari datum est, etsi ex pluribus Patribus tàm Græcis, quam Latinis, Theodoreto, Cyrillo, Prospero Aquitanico, Fulgentio aliisque colligi adducique possent uberrima, nobis tamen hôc locô suffecerit in duorum, diffusioris cùm eruditionis, tùm Commentationis atque eloquii sacri, palmam, & Antecessoribus, & Successoribus, facilè præripientium Patrum Sententiis acquievisse. Alter horum Orientalis, Occidentalis Ecclesiæ alter Doctor kat' exochēn communisque & meretur dici, & vulgò consuevit appellari, S. CHRYSOSTOMUM intelligo, & S. AUGUSTINUM.
english: §.IX: for the FIFTH century — last of the purer Evangelical ages — many Fathers could be cited, but two snatch the palm.
East and West’s doctors par excellence: Chrysostom and Augustine.

source_text: PRIOR uti à Mysteriis omnibus Carnalitatem, sic à S. Cœna, corporis Christi carnalem tùm præsentiam, tùm participationem, semoturus, Homil. 45. in Johannem ita commentatur: Mysteria, inquit, non sunt carnaliter, sed interioribus oculis, i. e. spiritualiter, consideranda & contemplanda; Hujusmodi enim est Mysteriorum natura. Et paucis interjectis, sic pergit: Sicut in Baptismo, sensibili aqua elemento, intelligibile Regenerationis donum; ita etiam INTELLIGIBILE hoc corporis & sanguinis Christi donum, non corporea aut sensibili aliquâ actione, sed spirituali fidei intelligentiâ, animo atque mente percipitur.
english: Chrysostom (Hom. 45 on John) strips carnality from the mysteries and from the Supper’s carnal presence and participation.

Mysteries are for interior eyes — spiritual. As baptism’s sensible water carries an intelligible regeneration-gift, so the intelligible gift of body and blood is received by faith’s spiritual intelligence, not by bodily action.

source_text: POSTERIOR verò, Veritatem in hoc puncto divinam omnem elocuturus (1) Verba Institutionis S. Cœnæ Essentialia: Accipite edite, Hoc est Corpus meum, figurata esse, nec sine Metonymiæ tropo accipienda, satis clarè pronuntiat, quando contra Adimantum Lib. 12. ita scribit: Dominus non dubitavit dicere, Hoc est corpus meum, cum signum daret corporis sui, subnexa insuper ratione Lib. 2. de Doctrina Christ. c. 16., ob quam in mandato Christi, de manducando corpore suo, aliisque similibus, Figura necessariò subintelligenda sit; si, inquit Augustinus, præceptiva locutio aut flagitium aut facinus videtur jubere, aut utilitatem aut beneficium vetare, figurata est. Nisi manducaveritis, inquit Christus, carnem Filii Hominis & sanguinem biberitis, non habebitis Vitam in vobis, facinus vel flagitium videtur jubere, FIGURA EST ERGO, præcipiens, Passioni Domini esse communicandum & suaviter atque utiliter recondendum in memoria, quod pro nobis caro ejus crucifixa & vulnerata est.
english: Augustine (1): the essential Institution words (‘Take, eat, This is my Body’) are figurative — not without metonymy (Against Adimantus 12; Doctr. Chr. 2.16).
If a command seems to order a crime, it is figurative: ‘Unless you eat my flesh…’ seems criminal — therefore it is a FIGURE commanding communion in the Passion and memory of the crucified flesh.

source_text: (2) Figuratam interim Christi locutionem, veram corporis ejus in Cœna S., vel præsentiam, vel participationem, neutiquam è medio tollere dicit: Jam, ait Augustinus, Christiani, peracti sacrificii memoriam, celebrant, sacrosanctâ oblatione & participatione Corporis & sanguinis Christi, Lib. 20. contra Faustum cap. 18. confer. cap. 21. At verò (3.) Præsentiam atque participationem Corporis Christi in Cœna, Spirituales facit: Spiritualiter inquit, intelligite quæ locutus sum (Christum hic loquentem introducens); Nam hoc Corpus, quod videtis, manducaturi estis & bibituri illum sanguinem, quem fusuri sunt, qui me crucifigent, Sacramentum vobis aliquod commendavi, SPIRITUALITER intellectum vivificabit vos in Psalm. 98. Item Tractatu 25. in Johannem: Ut quid paras dentes & Ventrem: Crede & manducasti.
english: Augustine (2): the figure does not remove true presence or participation — Christians celebrate with sacrosanct oblation and participation of Body and blood (Against Faustus 20.18).
(3) Presence and participation are spiritual: understand spiritually; the sacrament understood spiritually quickens (Ps. 98). Tract. 25 John: Why prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten.

source_text: Idque (4.) cum exclusione præsentiæ localis & participationis oralis: Ita enim Tract. 30. in Johannem pergit: Donec seculum finiatur, sursum est Dominus, sed tamen, hic etiam nobiscum est Veritas Domini. CORPUS ENIM DOMINI, IN QUO RESURREXIT, UNO LOCO esse oportet, veritas autem ejus ubique diffusa est. Et Tract. 50. in Johann. Christus absens etiam præsens est: Corpus enim suum intulit cœlo, Majestatem non abstulit mundo. Et Tract. I. in Epistolam Johannis. Dominum jam in cælo sedentem MANU (ore) contrectare non possumus, sed Fide contingere.
english: Augustine (4): local presence and oral handling shut out — until the age ends the Lord is above, yet His Truth is here with us.

The Lord’s risen body must be in ONE PLACE; His truth is everywhere. Absent yet present: body in heaven, Majesty not withdrawn. We cannot handle Him in heaven with hand or mouth — only touch by Faith.

source_text: Etiam (5) cum exclusione participationis Corporis Christi, quod ad indignos, i. e. Impœnitentes atq; incredulos attinet. Sic enim expressè discriminat inter manducationem credentium Christi Discipulorum, & Judæ proditoris Christi: Discipuli, ait, manducabant panem Dominum; Judas panem Domini, contra Dominum, Tract. 59. in Johannem.
english: Augustine (5): the unworthy (impenitent, unbelieving) are excluded from participation of the Body.
Disciples ate the bread the Lord; Judas ate the Lord’s bread against the Lord (Tract. 59 on John).
Stop before §.X (sixth century onward — decline; Gelasius still holding).

source_text: §. X. Meliorum Seculorum finem attigimus, deterioremque initium, SEXTUM puta, quô res Veritasque Christiana in pejus ruere cœpit; Quare non præter rem Gerhard. Theodorus Mejerus, Sectionem suam sextam, Christianæ Religionis Seculi sexti Historiam exhibentem, p. 164. ita inchoat §. I.
english: §.X: we have reached the end of the better ages and the start of the worse — the SIXTH — when Christian truth began to rush downhill.
Mejerus opens his sixth section (Christian Religion of the sixth age, p. 164) with that framing.

source_text: Et hactenus Statum Religionis Christianæ Seculo quidem V. bonum, meliorem Seculo quarto, optimum tribus primis seculis, cognovimus, nunc demum subsequuntur secula, quibus in deterius ruere incipit Christianismus, atque novam prorsus induit faciem. Deterior hic Religionis Christianæ Status, qui Seculo VI. capit, primis temporibus fuit malus, mediis pejor, ultimis vero, ante reformationem, pessimus. Atque sic à primordiis Ecclesiæ Christi usque ad Reformationem, sex distincta intervalla, seu ætates religionis christianæ, in historia annotamus. Primis quinque seculis sensim & nonnunquam sine sensu gliscere, seculo denique sexto, cursu quodam velociore atque palam ruere in Christianâ religione novos errores ac superstitiones observamus. Etiamsi verò, observante Mejero, Seculo sextô, velociori quôdam cursu novi errores ac superstitiones irruere ingruereque cœperint,
english: Mejerus: Age V still good; IV better; the first three best — then ages follow in which Christianity puts on a new, worse face.
Six ages from the Church’s beginnings to the Reformation: errors creep in the first five; in the sixth they rush in faster and openly.

source_text: fuerunt tamen etiam hộc Seculô nonnulli, qui & veritati Eucharisticæ constantiores adhesêre. Hos inter GELASIUS & nominis hujus & dignitatis Papalis propemodum primus numerandus, in cujus scripto quodam, Eutychi & Nestorio opposito, à Gratiano verò allegato, de Consecrat. Distinct. 2. cap. 12. hæc inter alia legimus, pro veritate, & contra Transsubstantiationem, facientia:
english: Yet even in this age some clung more constantly to Eucharistic truth.
Among them GELASIUS — almost first of the papal name and dignity — in a writing against Eutyches and Nestorius (Gratian, de Consecrat. Dist. 2 c. 12), for truth and against Transubstantiation.

source_text: Certè Sacramenta, ait, quæ sumimus, corporis & sanguinis Christi, DIVINA RES est, propter quod & per eadem, divinæ naturæ consortes efficimur: Non tamen esse desinit substantia & natura Panis & Vini; Certè IMAGO ET SIMILITUDO CORPORIS ET SANGUINIS Christi in actione Mysteriorum celebrantur.
english: Gelasius: the Sacraments of Christ’s body and blood that we take are a DIVINE THING — through them we share the divine nature.
Yet bread and wine do not cease to be in substance and nature; in the Mysteries’ action the IMAGE AND LIKENESS of body and blood are celebrated.

source_text: Gelasio suffragatur ejusdem Seculi Episcopus Hermianensis FOECUNDUS, Justiniani Imperatoris tempore florens, (Vid. Petavii Rationarium tempor. part. 1. Lib. 7. cap. 7. & 8.) Hic Librô nonô Operis sui, improprietatem verborum Christi æquè ac Spiritualem ejus in S. Eucharistia præsentiam, hisce significatum it: SACRAMENTUM inquit, corporis & sanguinis Christi, quod est in pane & poculo consecrato, corpus ejus & sanguinem dicimus: Non quod PROPRIE corpus ejus sit panis, & poculum sanguis, sed quod in se MYSTERIUM corporis sanguinisque continent, secutus scil. Doctrinam, de corporis Christi naturali localique absentiâ in terris, VIGILII Episcopi Tridentini, triginta propemodum annis illo senioris,
english: Foecundus of Hermiane (same age; Justinian’s time) seconds Gelasius: Christ’s words are improper speech; presence in the Eucharist is spiritual.

We call the sacrament in consecrated bread and cup His body and blood — not that bread is PROPERLY body or cup blood, but that they contain the MYSTERY — following Vigilius of Trent on the body’s natural local absence on earth.

source_text: cujus contra Eutychen & Nestorium disputantis verba notatu dignissima, omnem hac de re sententiam Reformatorum exponunt: Dei filius, ait ille, secundum humanitatem recessit à nobis, secundum divinitatem ait nobis: Ecce ego vobiscum sum. Per formam servi, quam abstulit à nobis in cælum, ABSENS EST NOBIS; per formam Dei, qua non recedit à nobis, in terris præsens est nobis, Lib. 1. Itemque Lib. 4. Caro Christi, quando in terra fuit, non erat utique in cælo, & nunc quia in cælo est, NON EST UTIQUE IN TERRA. Apparet unum eundemque Christum, UTRIUSQUE ESSE NATURÆ, & esse quidem ubique, secundum NATURAM divinitatis suæ, & loco contineri, secundum NATURAM humanitatis suæ.
english: Vigilius (against Eutyches and Nestorius) states the Reformers’ sentence: according to humanity the Son withdrew; according to divinity He is with us.

By the servant-form taken into heaven He is ABSENT; by the form of God He is present on earth. Flesh once on earth was not in heaven; now in heaven it is NOT ON EARTH. One Christ of BOTH NATURES — everywhere by divinity, place-bound by humanity.
Stop before §.XI (seventh century; Isidore).

source_text: §. XI. De SECULO SEPTIMO quid nobis sperare liceat, quod ad confirmationem veritatis Eucharisticæ attinet, in aprico ponit Inscriptio à paulò ante allegato Mejero Helmstadiensi, eidem, hunc in modum, præfixa: In seculum septimum, communi doctorum Protestantium sententia, referuntur initia Anti-Christi, tam Orientalis quam Occidentalis: Unde insignes hôc seculo Status Religionis Christianæ passus est mutationes. Et quidem in Oriente non tam hæresis aliqua, aut secta, sed totius Religionis Christianæ occurrit excidium. In Occidente Pontifices Romani, Antichristiana dominatione statum Ecclesiæ Religionis Christianæ hactenus liberiorem, nunc servilem facere satagunt. §. 1. 52. p. 170. Cui præfixæ Inscriptioni accedat suffixa Paragraphi tertii: Veritatis testes, qui hoc seculo, mysterio iniquitatis contradixerunt, & Religionis Christianæ sinceritatem propagaverunt, numero oppido pauci fuerunt, quorum etiam aliquos ineptæ quæstiones occuparunt & exercuerunt, necessariâ doctrina neglectâ: Est enim Seculum VII. sterile scriptorum bonæ frugis. p. m. 171.
english: §.XI: what hope for the SEVENTH age confirming Eucharistic truth? Mejerus puts it in the open.

Protestant doctors refer Anti-Christ’s beginnings (East and West) to this age — East: ruin of whole religion; West: Rome drives the Church toward servitude. Truth-witnesses few; Age VII sterile of good writers.

source_text: Ut proinde nemini mirum videri debeat, si unum solum ISIDORUM, Episcopum Hispalensem, Veritatis hoc loco à nobis statuminandæ Possessorem advocemus, Lib. 1. de Offic. Eccles. c. 8. ita scribentem: Panis quia confirmat corpus nostrum, ideò corpus Christi nuncupatur, vinum autem quia sanguinem operatur in carne, ideo ad sanguinem Christi refertur. Hæc autem duo sunt visibilia; sanctificata tamen per Spiritum S. IN SACRAMENTUM DIVINI CORPORIS (non in substantiam corporis & sanguinis Christi) transeunt: Panis enim quem frangimus corpus Christi est, qui dicit, Ego sum Panis Vivus; Vinum autem, sanguis ejus est, & hoc est quod scriptum est, Ego sum vitis vera.
english: So Strimesius summons one alone: ISIDORE of Seville (de Offic. Eccles. 1.8).

Bread is called Christ’s body because it confirms ours; wine referred to His blood because it works blood in the flesh — visible things that, sanctified, pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of body and blood).

source_text: Et adhuc clariùs Lib. 6. Etymolog. cap. 12. Sicuti enim substantia panis & vini visibilis, nutrit hominem exteriorem, ita verbum Christi, qui est panis vivus, PER PARTICIPATIONEM FIDEI, recreat animas fidelium. Quæ verba è Libris Isidori hodie impressis expuncta, à Bertramo Presbytero conservata nobis, Joh. Dunelmensis, Tract. crebrius cit. p. m. 84. observat.
english: Clearer still (Etymolog. 6.12): visible bread and wine nourish the outer man; Christ’s word, the living bread, recreates faithful souls THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH.
Those words are struck from today’s printed Isidore — preserved by Bertram the Presbyter (John of Durham notes).

source_text: Isidoro Hispalensi sese proximè adjungit VENERABILIS BEDA, Britannicarum Insularum Doctor celeberrimus, quanquam octavo demum seculô Nomen ejus inclaruerit, non Eucharisticam duntaxat veritatem, Comment. in 22. Ps. palam hisce confessus: Loco carnis & sanguinis agni, substituit Christus Sacramentum carnis suæ & sanguinis, in FIGURA panis & vini. Item, Comm. in Psal. 3. Dedit in Cœna discipulis FIGURAM sacrosancti corporis & sanguinis sui;
english: Next to Isidore: the VENERABLE BEDE (British Isles’ doctor; name famous mainly in the eighth age).

On Ps. 22: in place of the lamb’s flesh and blood Christ put the Sacrament of His flesh and blood in the FIGURE of bread and wine. On Ps. 3: at the Supper He gave the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood.

source_text: Sed & falsitatem, i. e. corporalem Christi, sive corporis ejus, tàm in terris hisce, quàm in Cœna S., præsentiam, seriò detestatus: Christus, inquit, ad patrem, post resurrectionem, Victor adscendens, Ecclesiam CORPORALITER reliquit, quam tamen nunquam divinæ præsidio præsentiæ destituit. Comment. in Marcum Lib. 4. cap. 13. Et in Joh. cap. 14. A quibus, ait, homo abscedebat Dominus, eos non relinquebat idem ipse Christus homo & Deus. Ergo ibat per id, quod homo erat, & manebat per id, quod Deus erat. Ibat per id, quod uno loco erat, & manebat per id, quod ubique erat.
english: Bede also seriously detests the falsehood of a corporal presence of Christ or His body — on earth or in the Sacred Supper.

Ascending Victor after the resurrection He left the Church CORPORALLY, yet never without divine presence. As man He went; as God He remained — going as in one place, remaining as everywhere (Mark 4.13; John 14).

source_text: Denique in cap. Joh. sextum: Quisquis vivere vult, credat in Christum, manducet SPIRITUALITER SPIRITUALEM CIBUM incorporeum corporis Christi, & non sit putridum membrum.
english: On John 6: whoever would live, believe in Christ and eat SPIRITUALLY the SPIRITUAL FOOD — the incorporeal of Christ’s body — and not be a putrid member.
Stop before §.XII (eighth century; Damascene / image-age).

source_text: §. XII. Ceterum OCTAVUM SECULUM, quod unà cum Septimo, divinæ iræ Seculum rectissimè appellitat prædictus Mejerus, initio Sectionis suæ nonæ p. 177, Uti Imaginum in templis & oratoriis sacris defensione, ita & veritatis Eucharisticæ in falsitatem, id est, panis & vini, in Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, immutatione, utrâque argumentis rationi falsæ & Sapientiæ humanæ unicè debitis, innixâ, quin multis præterea, tam in Doctrina, quàm in ritibus, sapientium sibi visorum mortalium inventis commentisque, famosum est (Quo de videatur Spanhemius noster, Hist. Imag. Sect. I. §. XI. p. 33.)
english: §.XII: the EIGHTH age — with the Seventh, Mejerus’s age of divine wrath — is infamous for defending images in temples and for mutating Eucharistic truth into falsehood.
Bread and wine into Body and Blood, each propped on false reason and human wisdom, plus many mortal inventions in doctrine and rites (Spanheim, Hist. Imag.).

source_text: adeo, ut Christianæ istius Seculi Ecclesiæ, ex majori sui parte consideratæ, applicari illud debeat, quod Paulus de Ethnicis ad Romanos scribit: Proptereà, quòd cùm Deum noverint, tamen ut Deum non glorificaverunt, sed vani facti sunt in ratiocinationibus suis & obtenebratum est Cor eorum, intelligentiâ carens, cùm se dictitant Sapientes, stulti facti sunt & mutarunt gloriam DEI incorruptibilis in efformatas omnis generis imagines panisque spumam, olim à posteris suis adorandam.
english: So far that Paul’s charge against the Gentiles (Romans) fits most of this age’s Christian Church:

Knowing God they did not glorify Him; claiming to be wise they became fools and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for fashioned images of every kind — and the foam of bread for posterity to adore.

source_text: Certe ipse Johannes Damascenus, illius Seculi, præ ceteris, Doctor Celebratissimus, deque Orthodoxia, in suis de ea libris quatuor, ad hodiernorum, Orthodoxiæ monopolium sibi vindicantium, gloriatus modum, uti pro imaginibus scribendo decertavit acriter (annotantibus id Chronologis Celeberrimis, Calvisio & Helviso ad annum Christi 728. & 730., paginis mihi 625. & 112.) ita ad Pontificios de Eucharistia sentiendi loquendique modos erroneos divertit, seu potius hisce prælusisse censendus est, quando de fide Orthodoxa lib. 4. cap. 4. ita scribit: Quemadmodum naturaliter panis per commestionem, & vinum atque aqua, per bibitionem, in corpus & sanguinem edentis & bibentis commutantur & aliud fiunt corpus, præter prius illud corpus; Sic panis & vinum & aqua propositionis, per invocationem & adventum Sancti Spiritûs, supernaturaliter COMMUTANTUR in corpus & sanguinem Christi, à Theophylacto idcirco emendandus, notante Wittakero, pag. 102.
english: John of Damascus, that age’s chief Doctor of Orthodoxy, fought sharply for images (Calvisius/Helvisus note ~728–730) — and turned toward (or rather preluded) Pontifical errors on the Eucharist.

Orthodox Faith 4.4: as bread and wine naturally change into the eater’s body, so the bread, wine, and water of the proposition are supernaturally CHANGED into Christ’s body and blood — Theophylact must emend him (Whittaker).

source_text: aliarum quoque plurimarum innovationum & Terminorum, scholasticorum deinceps dictorum, temerè satis sanctæ Religioni & Theologiæ Christianæ intrusorum reus, quin Autor postulatus à sæpius laudato Mejero, paragraphum tertium Sectionis suæ octavæ ita exorso: Capita prætereà hôc seculo nova ratio tractandi doctrinam religionis Christianæ, auctore Damasceno, qui eam, ad modum scientiæ, primus tradere instituit. Hic, omissis quibusdam momentosis articulis, spinosas & inutiles quæstiones in Theologiam intulit, novas doctorum opiniones, ut religionis Christianæ dogmata proposuit, rarius ad Scripturam provocavit; formam sanorum verborum neglexit, formulis philosophorum potiùs, quam theologorum antiquorum & scripturæ utens. Et quia plerique postsecuti Doctores istam tractandi rationem sunt amplexi, sensim simplex veterum de religione Christianâ doctrinæ ratio, mutata est in scholasticas disputationes. p. 174. & 175.
english: Guilty also of many later ‘scholastic’ terms rashly thrust into sacred theology — Mejerus names Damascene author of a new scientific method of treating Christian doctrine.

Thorny useless questions; new opinions as dogmas; rare appeal to Scripture; philosopher-formulas over sound words — and followers gradually turned the ancients’ simple doctrine into scholastic disputations.

source_text: Intereà deviantibus ita à veritate multijuga, Damasceno & asseclis quàm plurimis, eodem seculo Octavo, errorum flumini, universam Ecclesiam inundaturo, sese opposuere verè Orthodoxi, i. e. Scripturæ S. pressius inhærentes haud pauci, dum sedibus suis undique exciti, Constantinopolim convenerunt Concilium, ab hac Civitate denominatum quintum, Græcis Oecumenicum septimum dictum, sub Constant. Copronymo & Leone Isaurico, à varia fama & æstimationis suæ proterva laceratione per Spanhemium nostrum vindicatis, celebratum; Hi per FIGURAM CORPORIS CHRISTI quam in Cœna statuebant, omnem figurarum seu Imaginum omnium usum sacrum abrogare éque medio tollere conabantur,
english: Meanwhile truly Orthodox (Scripture-clinging) opposed Damascene’s flood of errors in the same Eighth age.

Gathered at Constantinople (fifth / Greeks’ seventh Oecumenical; Copronymus and Leo Isaurian — Spanheim vindicates them): by the FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY they set in the Supper they tried to abolish every sacred use of images.

source_text: eo tamen nomine passuri contradictionem gravissimam, sub pessimâ Irene, ab Iconolatris Nicænis, qui panem, in S. Cœna, non Figuram Corporis, sed ipsum corpus Christi, per Conversionem esse, acerrimè contendebant, id quod fusiùs Annotat. 3. §. 3. indicavimus.
english: Under worst Irene they met heaviest contradiction from Nicaean Iconolaters, who contend the Supper bread is not the Figure of the Body but Christ’s body itself by Conversion (see Annotat. 3 §.3).
Stop before §.XIII (ninth century; Charlemagne / Bertram reclaiming).

source_text: §. XIII. Etsi verò ab hoc, ad Reformationis usque tempora perversissima, Nicænorum tam de incorruptibilis Dei in Imaginem hominis corruptibilis, quàm de panis Eucharistici in Corporis Christi Substantiam Transmutatione agraphô quin antigraphô, Sententia primas tenuerit, longe lateque disseminanda; inventi tamen etiam SECULO NONO, hinc inde sunt, qui utrique Transsubstantiationi pro virili reclamarent. Enimverò circa ipsum Seculi Noni ingressum, divus Imperator CAROLUS, jure suô MAGNUS appellatus, sicuti imaginum venerationem usumque sacrum, per Francofurtense Concilium, intra certos saltem limites, coërcuit Anno 794.; ita de Eucharistia quoque sanorum Christi verborum formam, in Epistola sua ad Alcuinum, luculenter satis hisce expressit: Cœnando, inquit, cum Discipulis Christus, panem fregit & calicem pariter dedit iis in FIGURAM corporis & sanguinis sui, nobisque profuturum magnum exhibuit Sacramentum.
english: §.XIII: though Nicaean sentences on image-transmutation and bread-into-Body held first place until the Reformation, the NINTH age still found reclaimers against both Transubstantiations.

Around its entrance CHARLES THE GREAT restrained image-veneration (Frankfurt 794) and, to Alcuin, said Christ gave bread and cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood — a great Sacrament for our profit.

source_text: Procedente Seculô & ad medium sui assurgente, Caroli M. Nepos, initiô Rex Franciæ, mox Imperator quoque sat inclitus, CAROLUS CALVUS, veritatis Evangelicæ, etiam in doctrina de Eucharistia percupidus, tum Bertramo Presbytero, tùm Erigena Scoto, de corpore & sanguine Domini Tractatus scribere jussit, ex quorum priori, cum adhuc in manibus eruditorum versetur, quasdam propositiones veritatem Eucharisticam illustraturas, hic adduxisse operæ pretium ducimus.
english: Mid-century: CHARLES THE BALD, eager for Evangelical truth on the Eucharist, ordered Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write treatises on the Lord’s body and blood.
Bertram’s still circulates among the learned — Strimesius draws propositions that illustrate the Eucharistic truth.

source_text: Ac (1) quidem, verborum Institutionis Christi improprietatem edocturus Bertramus: Panis vinumque, ait ille, FIGURATE Christi corpus & sanguis existunt. Itemque: Iste panis & calix, qui corpus & sanguis Christi nominantur, memoriam representant Dominicæ Passionis sive mortis, quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio dixit: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Quod exponens Apostolus Paulus ait: quotiescunque manducaveritis panem & calicem biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, donec veniat. Docemur à Salvatore nec non à S. Paulo Apostolo, quod iste panis & iste sanguis, qui super altare ponuntur, in FIGURAM sive memoriam Dominicæ mortis ponuntur, ut quod gestum est in præterito, præsenti revocet memoria, ut illius passionis memores effecti, per eam efficiamur divini muneris consortes, per quam sumus à morte liberati.
english: Bertram (1): Institution words are improper — bread and wine exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood.

Named body and blood, they represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion; set on the altar in the FIGURE or memory of His death, so present memory of what was done may make us partakers of the divine gift.

source_text: (II) Naturale corpus Christi, modô corporali, in Cena non præsens esse, inculcaturus, significantissimè ita scribit: Corpus & Sanguis quod in Ecclesia geritur (i. e. quod manibus Ministrorum in Ecclesia tractatur, manibusque & ore accipitur) differt ab illo corpore & sanguine quod in Christi corpore per resurrectionem jam glorificatum cognoscitur: Et hoc Corpus (nempe Eucharisticus panis) SIGNUM est & SPECIES; illud verò ipsa veritas. Hoc enim geritur, donec ad illud perveniatur. Ubi verò ad illud perventum fuerit, hoc removebitur. Apparet ita quod multâ inter se differentia separantur, quantum est inter pignus & eam rem pro qua pignus traditur, & quantum inter imaginem & rem cujus est imago, & quantum inter speciem & veritatem. Hic nemo arbitretur contendere Bertramum, umbram, & non veritatem in sacramento sumi (perpetuò enim, ut paulò post dicemus, cibo Spirituali potuque Fidelium animas in S. Cœna pasci allaborat inculcare); Sed quod negat hic Bertramus, istud solum est: Verum & naturale corpus Christi Ore corporis manducari.
english: Bertram (II): Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode — what ministers handle differs from the glorified body; the Eucharistic bread is SIGN and SPECIES, that is the truth itself (pledge vs thing; image vs reality).
He does not deny truth taken in the sacrament — souls are fed with Spiritual food and drink — he denies only that the true natural body is eaten with the body’s Mouth.

source_text: (III) Nec naturale corpus Christi, Corporaliter, seu Oraliter, in Cœna manducari evicturus, quæstionem hanc ex professo proponit: Utrum ipsum corpus quod de Maria natum & passum, mortuum & sepultum, quodque ad Dextram Patris residet, sit, quod ore Fidelium per Sacramentorum mysterium, in Ecclesia quotidie sumatur? Et respondet ex Ambrosio per Scripturam loquente… Non secundum hoc, quod videtur, quod corporaliter sumitur, quod dente premitur, quod fauce glutitur… æterna vita substantiam subministrat… Interim tamen (IV.) Spiritualem corporis Christi tàm præsentiam quam participationem pleno ore confessurus, in Responsione ad priorem Imperatoris quæstionem: Num Mysteriôso quôdam modô corpus Christi in Cœna à Fidelibus sumatur? occupatus, inter alia ita respondet: Quandoquidem omnium confessione corpus & sanguis Christi in Cœna sumitur, necesse est, panem & vinum in melius quoddam transiisse, mutationemque hanc non CORPORALITER, sed SPIRITUALITER contigisse, ut jam nunc rectè dicatur, mutationem dictam FIGURATIVE factam esse, subque tegumento corporalis panis & vini, SPIRITUALE CORPUS ET SPIRITUALEM SANGUINEM Christi, actu præsentem esse… Quoniam est SPIRITUALIS ESCA, est SPIRITUALIS POTUS, spiritualiter pascens & æternæ satietatis vitam tribuens.
english: Bertram (III): the body born of Mary, dead, risen, at the Father’s right, is not what teeth press and throats swallow daily — that corporal intake does not supply eternal life.

(IV) Yet he confesses Spiritual presence and participation: bread and wine pass into something better not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY — under corporal covering the SPIRITUAL BODY AND BLOOD are actually present; SPIRITUAL FOOD and DRINK.

source_text: Adhuc disertius Johannem Scotum Erigenam, omnem Bertrami, Coævi sui & Comilitionis, à Carolo Calvo unà evocati, de Eucharistia traditam veritatem enunciasse scriptoque comprehendisse, etsi ejus Tractatus injuria temporum deperditus, vel potiùs Pontificis Romani & aliorum malevolorum perverso zelô, traditus Vulcano sit, fidem faciunt alia Viri hujus Scripta, de Divisione naturæ, per Oxonienses, Anno superioris seculi 81. ab interitu vindicata… Aliorum Seculi Noni Scriptorum de Eucharistia Orthodoxorum testimonia, Amalarii puta, Rabani Mauri, Walafridi Strabonis, ut & ipsius Bertrami, contra Pontificios vindicata vide apud Dunelmensem à p. 88. ad p. 97.
english: Erigena, Bertram’s coeval fellow summoned by Charles the Bald, stated the same Eucharistic truth — his treatise lost (or burned by hostile zeal), but On the Division of Nature (Oxford recovery) and other writings make faith.
See also Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself vindicated in Durham pp. 88–97. Stop before §.XIV (tenth century).

source_text: §. XIV. SECULUM X, à Baronio in Annalibus atrô satis carbone notatum est, ob boni sterilitatem, ferreum, mali exundantis deformitatem, plumbeum, ob inopiam denique Scriptorum, obscurum nuncupatum, BELLARMINI etiam indignabundam hanc exclamationem promeritum: Vide Seculum infelix, in quo nulli Scriptores illustres, nulla Concilia, Pontifices parum solliciti de republica, subintellige Ecclesiastica;
english: §.XIV: Baronius marks the TENTH age with black coal — iron for sterility of good, leaden for overflowing evil, obscure for want of writers.
Bellarmine’s cry: unhappy age — no illustrious writers, no councils, pontiffs little solicitous for the ecclesiastical republic.

source_text: Habuit tamen etiam genuina de S. Cœna explicationis Professores & testes, ab Erigero Abbate Loviensi congestos, uti refert sæpè memoratus Cosinus Episcopus Anglus, ipsemet Anglorum suorum istius temporis Homilias, publice etiam in Ecclesiis Anglicis olim legi solitas, in medium adducens & ex Concionibus istis, p. 98. verba allegans, Bertrami assertis exacte parallela:
english: Yet it still had professors and witnesses of a genuine Supper explanation, collected by Erigerus of Louvain.
Cosin (English bishop) brings into the midst English homilies once read publicly in churches — words at p. 98 exactly parallel to Bertram.

source_text: Nam hunc in modum Homilia una, quæ Paschalis est, populum instituit: Multum interest inter corpus in quo passus est Christus, & corpus quod in hostia consecratur, corpus quidem in quo Christus passus est, ex Mariæ Virginis carne natum est, ac sanguine, ossibus, cute, nervis & membris humanis atque anima rationali constat; At SPIRITUALE ejus CORPUS, quod Hostiam appellamus, ex multis granis collectum est, sine sanguine, ossibus, membris, sine anima. Deinde Christi corpus quod semel mortuum est & à morte resurrexit, deinceps nunquam morietur, sed æternum est & impassibile, Hostia verò ista temporarie est corruptibilis in varias partes distributa, dentibus confecta & in ventrem transmissa, denique Mysterium hoc, pignus est & FIGURA; Christi corpus est veritas ipsa.
english: Paschal Homily: much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body consecrated in the host.

The suffered body has Mary’s flesh, blood, bones, soul; the SPIRITUAL BODY we call Host is from many grains, without blood or soul — temporal, chewable; the Mystery is pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.

source_text: Quod videtur, panis est; quod SPIRITUALITER intelligitur, Vita est.
english: The Homily hinge: eyes meet bread.
Faith understanding meets Life — spiritual reading of the same host.

source_text: Altera verò Wulfini Episcopi Homilia, concisè equidem, at nervosè admodum sic informat: Hostia illa (scil. Sacramentalis) est Christi corpus, non CORPORALITER, sed SPIRITUALITER, non corpus in quo passus est Christus, sed corpus de quo locutus est, quando panem & vinum in hostiam consecravit.
english: Bishop Wulfinus’s Homily, brief but sinewy: the sacramental Host is Christ’s body not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY.
Not the body in which Christ suffered, but the body of which He spoke when He consecrated bread and wine into the host.

source_text: Hisce verbis tam veram & realem corporis Christi in S. Cena præsentiam, quàm unicum hujus præsentiæ genuinumque modum, à Christo Johan. VI. definitum, i. e. spiritualem, disertè inculcans. Quorsum etiam postrema Homiliæ hujus allegata verba interpretanda veniunt, ut nimirum non corporis Christi passi & crucifixi præsentiam realem, sed corporalem duntaxat, spirituali, in Homilia asserta, oppositam, in Cena S. inficientur.
english: These words inculcate both true real presence in the Sacred Supper and the sole genuine mode Christ defined in John 6 — the spiritual.
The Homily’s close does not deny real presence of the suffered body — only corporal presence opposed to the spiritual. Stop before §.XV (Hildebrandine / Berengar).

source_text: §. XV. UNDECIMUM SECULUM Hildebrandinum vulgò dicitur, quod malitia & tyrannide Hildebrandi Papæ, seu Gregorii VII, omnium maximè infame est, cum Anti-Christianismus, i. e. Dominatus Tyrannisque Papalis, uti Seculo VII. in Bonifacio III, à Parricida Phoca, Episcopo Oecumenico constituto, plenam suam genituram consecutus, ita per artes Hildebrandinas Dictatusque hujus hominis insolentissimos, ad fastigium perductus est.
english: §.XV: the ELEVENTH age is commonly called Hildebrandine — most infamous by Pope Hildebrand (Gregory VII)’s malice and tyranny.
Papal dominion, born full under Boniface III (Phocas, Age VII), was driven to its summit by Hildebrandine arts and his insolent Dictates.

source_text: Quemadmodum verò Tyrannis Hildebrandi in ipsos Imperatores, maxime in Henricum IV. sæviit, ita quoque veritatis Eucharisticæ Confessorem ejus Seculi Celeberrimum BERENGARIUM ANDEGAVENSEM, quanquam alia de causa, involvit.
english: As Hildebrand’s tyranny raged against the Emperors — especially Henry IV — so it also involved that age’s most celebrated Eucharistic confessor.
BERENGAR OF TOURS — though for another cause.

source_text: Equidem, quinam præcisè hujus præstantissimi Confessoris de Sacra Cœna loquendi modi fuerint, non adeò in proclivi est decernere, quod Scripta hujus Viri, ab inimicorum suorum numerosa turba, penitus oppressa deletaque sunt; Quid quòd, concedi potest, hunc ipsum Berengarium, Transsubstantiatorum, unô alioque jam tum seculo cristas erigentium, importunitate, eò zeli adactum fuisse, ut de S. Cœna commentatus, Figuræ crebrius Typique & Signi, quam Antitypi Corporisque Christi, in eadem, omnibus Fidelibus communicantibus præsentissimi, mentionem injecerit; interim fatendum insimul est, veritati, quà rem & substantiam, firmiter adhæsisse eum, etiamsi per inhumanitatem adversariorum suorum, aliquando passus aliquid humani videatur.
english: His exact modes of speaking on the Sacred Supper are hard to pin down: enemies thoroughly suppressed and deleted his writings.

Under Transubstantiators’ pressure he more often stressed Figure, Type, and Sign than Antitype and Christ’s most-present Body — yet as to the thing and substance he firmly held the truth, even if adversaries’ cruelty sometimes made him look merely human.

source_text: Consensus ejus cum veritate partim ex Præceptoris ejus Fulberti, Carnotensis Episcopi, doctrina, partim ex Scriptis, Berengarii sententiæ oppositis hancque recensentibus, liquidò colligitur. Præceptoris doctrina ex Epistola ejus ad Adeodatum se clarè prodit, quando is inter cætera ita scribit: Mysterium fidei non visu corporeo, sed SPIRITU FIDEI in Eucharistia intuendum, quod enim substantia panis & vini apparet exterius, jam Corpus & Sanguis Christi fit interiùs; Non quod ore discernitur, sed quod affectu interiore degustatur. Exere igitur palatum fidei, dilata fauces spei, viscera charitatis extende & sume panem vitæ, interioris hominis alimentum. Iterum: De fide interioris hominis procedit divini gustus saporis, dum certè per salutaris Eucharistiæ infusionem influit Christus in viscera sumentis.
english: Consensus with the truth is clear from his teacher Fulbert of Chartres and from writings that oppose and review his sentence.

Fulbert to Adeodatus: look on the Eucharist’s faith-mystery not with bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH — outwardly bread and wine, inwardly Body and Blood; taste by interior affection; take the bread of life as the interior man’s food.

source_text: Inter opposita verò Berengario Scripta, Lanfranci Cantuariensis de Veritate Corporis Domini in Eucharistia, liber eminet, sequentia Berengarii verba repetens: Per Consecrationem altaris, panis & vinum fiunt Sacramentum Religionis, non desinunt esse quod erant, sed ut in aliud mutentur & fiant quæ non erant. Iterum: Sacrificium Ecclesiæ duobus constat, visibili sacramento & invisibili re sacramenti, i. e. corpore Christi. Rursus: Sacramenta sunt Visibilia rerum divinarum signacula, sed res ipsæ invisibiles in eo honorantur.
english: Among opposing books, Lanfranc of Canterbury On the Truth of the Lord’s Body stands out — and repeats Berengar’s own words.

By altar consecration bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion yet do not cease what they were; the Church’s sacrifice is visible sacrament plus invisible res (Christ’s body); sacraments are visible seals — the invisible things are what is honored.

source_text: Etsi verò ex his similibusque verbis, perperam à nonnullis, Berengarius Consubstantiationis Fautor & Patronus conjecturari consuevit, tamen annumerandum hisce minimè esse vel ipse Rupertus Abbas Tuitiensis, Consubstantiationis Crassioris Auctor, primus & præcipuus, fateri ultrò nullus verebitur, quando Berengarium non tantum errantium Antesignanum facit, sed & errorem ejus in eo collocat, quod Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, nudum rei sacræ signum voluerit haberi. Ita enim Rupertus Consubstantiator, Veritatis Confessores oppugnat: Illi autem quid dicant, quid pro argumento afferant, inquit, non habent, nisi quod aliqui ex iis, dum volunt Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Domini, solummodò signum esse sacræ rei, juxta errorem quondam Berengarii Turonensis … etiam B. Augustinum sentire ita putant (De Sacramento Eucharistico lib. 3. cap. 11. & 15.). Cetera de Berengario dicenda require suprà Annot. 3.
english: Some wrongly make Berengar a consubstantiation patron — even Rupert of Deutz (crasser consubstantiation’s chief author) refuses that and instead charges him with wanting a bare sign of the sacred thing.
Rupert attacks truth-confessors as having no argument but that bare-sign claim (ascribed also to Augustine). Rest on Berengar: see above, Annot. 3. Stop before §.XVI / next extract.

source_text: §. XVI. Berengarii, circa finem Seculi XI. piè demortui vestigia, docendo de S. Cœna, legit Asceticorum Scriptorum suo tempore facilè Princeps BERNHARDUS ABBAS CLARÆVALLENSIS sub ipsum ferè SECULI XIImi INITIUM, quo de testes sunt amplissimæ, binæ ejus Conciones indubitatò illi tribuendæ, altera de purificatione Mariæ, de S. Martino altera conscripta habitaque. In priori legeris, quòd Christi corpus in Mysterio (Cœnæ) cibus mentis sit, non ventris, proinde corporaliter non manducetur, sicut enim cibus est, ita & comedi intelligitur. In posteriori verò: Quod usque hodie eadem caro Christi, nobis, sed spiritualiter utique, non corporaliter exhibeatur.
english: §.XVI: near the opening of the XIIth age, BERNARD OF CLAIRVAUX — then prince of ascetic writers — walks Berengar’s footsteps on the Sacred Supper.
Two sermons (Purification of Mary; S. Martin): Christ’s body in the Mystery is food of the mind, not the belly — not eaten corporally; the same flesh is exhibited spiritually, not corporally.

source_text: Quô duplici effatô nervosissimâ omnem de corpore Christi in S. Cœna veritatem perorat, (1) faciendo istud cibum mentis eóque cibum Spiritualem, quodque idcirco (2) non corporaliter, sed spiritualiter præsens sit ac exhibeatur. Denique, (3.) Spiritualiter exhibitum, spiritualiter etiam proptereà manducetur, quia naturam rationemque cibi insequatur natura & ratio manducationis; Eóque, uti cibus corporalis, corporaliter assumtus, in corporis usum, ita cibus spiritualis, spiritualiter seu fide acceptus, in usum Spiritus, seu Animæ fidelis, i. e. in augmentum ac stabilimentum fidei communionisque cum Christo concedat. Confer Sermonem Bernhardi de S. Cœna in Caput VI. Johannis versum 56. 563.
english: Bernard’s sinewy triple on the Supper: (1) food of the mind = Spiritual food; (2) present and exhibited spiritually, not corporally;

(3) therefore eaten spiritually — eating matches the food’s nature: corporal food for the body, spiritual food received by faith for the faithful soul’s increase of faith and communion with Christ (cf. John 6:56).

source_text: Progressu Seculi, PETRUS DE BRUIS & Henricus quidam Monachus, in variis Galliæ partibus, pauloque post, PETRUS WALDUS Civis Lugdunensis, cum quodam Arnoldo socio, in Civitatibus Lugdunensi & Albigensi, veram, etiam de S. Cœna doctrinam, longè latèque prædicando disseminarunt, Sequacibus, ab istorum partim, partim à civitatum, in quibus illi docuêre, nominibus, Petro-Bruisiani, Arnoldistæ, Waldenses seu Waldenses, Pauperes de Lugduno, Albienses seu Albigenses appellatis, innumerisque à Pontificum Rom. assentatoribus, gravatis calumniis, quas tamen Nostrates efficacissimè toties quoties absterserunt ac diluerunt, interque hos doctissimus Armachanus, Libro sæpiùs citato de Success. ac Stat. Eccles. Occidentalium.
english: Later in the age PETER DE BRUIS and Henry the Monk, then PETER WALDO of Lyons with Arnold, preached the true Supper doctrine across Gaul — Lyons and Albi.
Followers called Petrobrusians, Arnoldists, Waldenses, Poor of Lyons, Albigenses — buried under papal flatterers’ calumnies that Our writers (Armachanus among the ablest) repeatedly washed off.

source_text: Sententia Waldensium istius temporis de S. Eucharistia, QUA VERBORUM INSTITUTIONIS CHRISTI INTERPRETATIONEM genuinam, vel ex ipsorum Pontificiorum relatione, cognoscere datur, puta tùm illius ætatis Auctoris Petri Lombardi, Sententiarum Lib. 4. Distinct. 10. Quæst. I. scribentis: Sunt quidam (Waldenses notat Auctor) asserentes in altari non esse corpus Christi vel sanguinem (intellige corporaliter præsentia); Sed ita Christum dixisse, hoc est Corpus meum, sicut Apostolus dixit, Petra autem erat Christus: dicunt ibi esse corpus Christi tantùm in Sacramento, h. e. in Signo; tum Junioris Rainerii, Sectam Waldensium omnibus aliis diuturniorem seu antiquiorem facientis, & ad tempora vel Sylvestri, vel ipsorum Apostolorum, referentis, quando in Summ. de Catharis & Leonistis refert, credidisse Waldenses, panem benedictum, in Figura quadam, dici corpus Christi, sicut dicitur, petra autem erat Christus.
english: Even Pontifical reporters preserve the Waldenses’ genuine reading of the Institution words.

Lombard: some say Christ’s body is not corporally on the altar — ‘This is my Body’ as ‘the Rock was Christ’; body only in the Sacrament/Sign. Rainerius: blessed bread called body in a Figure, as the rock was Christ.

source_text: QUA ASSERTAM VERAM CORPORIS CHRISTI IN S. CŒNA PRÆSENTIAM, ex Confessione eorum antiquiori, circa annum 1200. scripta, apud Hovedenum in Annalibus fol. 319. constat, in qua dicunt: Credimus, quod non salvatur, qui non manducat corpus Christi,
english: Yet they also assert true presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper.
Ancient confession ~1200 (Hoveden fol. 319): We believe he is not saved who does not eat the body of Christ.

source_text: etiam Transsubstantiationis portentosum vocabulum, teste Rainerio, sensu tamen Spirituali, haud defugientes, quando docent, Transsubstantiationem non fieri in manu conficientis, sed in ore dignè sumentis: Non, quasi panem in ore dignè sumentium in substantiam corporis Christi converti putassent, sed quod Sacramentum arbitrati sint etiam suo modo in ore dignè sumentium non tantum significativum (quale & in ore impiorum) sed & exhibitivum corporis & sanguinis Domini esse, quatenus sumtis, ore corporis fidelium, symbolis, simul & res significata, corpus & sanguis Christi, gustu fidei percipiuntur.
english: They do not flee the word Transubstantiation (Rainerius) — but take it spiritually: not in the consecrator’s hand, but in the worthy receiver’s mouth.

Not bread converted into substance there, but the Sacrament exhibitive (not only significative) of the Lord’s body and blood — symbols in the body’s mouth, the thing signified perceived by faith’s taste. Stop before §.XVII.

source_text: §. XVII. Sicuti verò SECULO XII, ita non minus XIII, & seqq. famosissimi Waldenses tàm vitàm, quàm doctrinam papalem, maximè de Transsubstantiatione, Innocentii III. auctoritate stabilitam, constanter & fortiter improbarunt, ut hoc nomine non præcipuum duntaxat locum inter veritatis Christianæ testes teneant, sed & primi Ecclesiæ Romanæ Reformatores dici mereantur.
english: §.XVII: in Ages XII and XIII and after, the famous Waldenses steadily rejected papal life and doctrine — above all Transubstantiation fixed by Innocent III.
For that they hold a chief place among Christian-truth witnesses and deserve to be called the Roman Church’s first Reformers.

source_text: Quanquam hanc ipsam ob causam, quòd generoso pectore sese Papatui opposuerunt, Curia Romana omnibus artibus viribusque eos in exterminium persecuta sit. Persecutionum genera crudelissima, Waldensibus, sub nominibus Bulgarorum & Albigensium, illata, ex multis hujus Seculi Historicis, prolixissimè enarrat doctissimus Armachanus, libro dicto cap. postremo, seu 10, à §. 18. & 27. ad finem usque capitis; in compendium omnia redegit, Confessionem eorum de S. Cœna subnectens summariam, Philippus Morneus,
english: Because they opposed the Papacy with generous courage, the Roman Curia hunted them to extermination with every art and force.
Armachanus narrates the cruellest persecutions under the names Bulgars and Albigenses; Morneus digests it and appends their summary Confession on the Sacred Supper.

source_text: postquam Innocentianum de Transsubstantiatione Decretum hisce præmisisset: Annotandum, inquit, Anno 1215, Innocentius III. Pontifex, in Concilio Lateranensi, decretalem promulgat, cujus initium: Firmiter credimus &c. quæ & Conversionis Formam definit, & huic monstro nomen imponit hisce verbis: Idem ipse Sacerdos & Sacrificium Jesus Christus, cujus corpus & sanguis in Sacramento Altaris, sub speciebus panis & vini, veraciter continentur: Transsubstantiatis pane in corpus & vino in Sanguinem potestate divina. Lib. 4. de Sacram. Missæ supposititio cap. 8. pag. 1649. initio.
english: Morneus first notes Innocent III’s Lateran decretal of 1215: Firmiter credimus…
It defines Conversion’s form and names the monster: Christ’s body and blood truly contained under bread and wine species — bread Transsubstantiated into body, wine into Blood by divine power.

source_text: At è contra (pergit Morneus) eâdem ætate in Delphinatu, Provincia Narbonensi, Occitana & Aquitana, Albigenses, & graviter hâc Pontificiâ doctrinâ offenduntur, & fortiter in eam insurgunt, secundum S. Scripturæ normam & antiquiorum Patrum usum, & credere, & docere, & vivere nihilominus rati. Pontifex itaque evertendorum quam convertendorum studiosior, Dominicum in speciem concionaturum mittit, at re vera, Leopoldum Ducem Austriæ & Simonem Comitem de Monteforti, cum ingentibus copiis vi oppressuros: pecuniam in Turcas collectam, Cruciatam vocabant, non sine sacrilegio interversam, in eos convertit; regiones porrò illas igne & ferrô vastat, nil aliud interim consecutus, quam ut totâ Europa sparsi, per Italiam, Germaniam, Bohemiam, Angliam, intima Galliæ, puriorem doctrinam, quam extinguere curabat, dispergerent.
english: Same age: Albigenses in Dauphiné, Narbonne, Occitania, Aquitaine are offended and rise against the pontifical doctrine by Scripture and the older Fathers’ use.
Innocent, keener to overthrow than convert, sends Dominic for show but Montfort and Leopold with armies — crusade money turned on them; fire and iron only scatter the purer doctrine across Europe.

source_text: Tandem subjicit Mornæus: Waldensium Confessio fidem faciat, quam consulere Lector ne dedignetur, quandoquidem omnia ferè Transsubstantiatorum argumenta solidè satis, pro tempore, ibi refutantur. Summa est: In S. Cœna secundum Institutionem Christi celebrata, fidelem, verum Christi corpus & sanguinem accipere: Panis interim aut vini naturam aut substantiam minimè mutari, verba enim Christi nullam Conversionem inducere; Et, si Elementum desineret, Sacramentum non ampliùs fore.
english: Morneus: consult the Waldensian Confession — it solidly answers most Transubstantiators’ arguments for its time.

Sum: in the Supper per Christ’s Institution the faithful receives Christ’s true body and blood; bread and wine nature/substance are not changed — His words induce no Conversion; if the element ceased, there would be no Sacrament.

source_text: Nihilo magis dici Christum sub speciebus existere, neque in pane, neque ex pane, neque cum pane. Non ibi esse Christum in corpore, naturali mansione, existenter & corporaliter, sed SPIRITUALITER, potenter, benedictè, in veritate; Secundum quam mansionem non aberit, neque abiturus sit à suis, in quorum cordibus habitat. Eos proinde solos, non alios CHRISTUM in Sacramentis recipere, qui intrinsècùs ejus spiritu vivificati sunt. Cæterum, corpus & sanguinem Christi à Fidelibus percipi debere, non autem sacrificari, aut venerationis causa, attolli, aut circumferri, pag. 1650.
english: Christ is not said to exist under the species — not in, from, or with the bread — not there corporally by natural abiding, but SPIRITUALLY, powerfully, blessedly, in truth, dwelling in His people’s hearts.

Only those inwardly vivified by His Spirit receive Christ in the Sacraments; body and blood are to be perceived by the Faithful — not sacrificed, elevated for veneration, or carried about. Stop before §.XVIII.

source_text: §. XVIII. A Waldensibus kat' exochēn sic dictis, i.e. in Gallia Seculo XII. natis, & XIII. propagatis, originem traxere WALDENSES ANGLI, SECULO XIV, unô nomine WICLEPHISTÆ dicti à Johanne Wiclepho, Doctore Anglo, qui floruit Anno 1370. Hujus Theses, tum Transsubstantiationi, tum Consubstantiationi oppositas, partim ex Concilio Constantiensi, in quo damnatæ sunt, partim ex IV. libro Trialog. cap. 7. & 43. de Sermone Domini in monte, collegit Franciscus Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico p. 57. & 58.
english: §.XVIII: from the Waldenses so called par excellence — born in Gaul in Age XII, spread in XIII — came the ENGLISH WALDENSES of Age XIV.
One name: Wycliffites, from John Wycliffe (English doctor, ~1370). Otrokocsi gathers his theses against both Transubstantiation and Consubstantiation from Constance (where condemned) and the Trialog.

source_text: TRANSSUBSTANTIATIONI ita contradicit Wicleph: Substantia panis manet in altari post Consecrationem & non definit esse panis. Item: Hostia consecrata, est naturaliter verus panis, & sacramentaliter corpus Christi. Item: Sicut Christus est simul Deus & homo, ita hostia consecrata est simul corpus Christi & verus panis: Quia est corpus Domini IN FIGURA, & verus panis IN NATURA.
english: Wycliffe against Transubstantiation: after consecration the bread’s substance remains on the altar — it does not cease to be bread.
The consecrated Host is naturally true bread and sacramentally Christ’s body — at once body and true bread, as Christ is at once God and man: the Lord’s body IN FIGURE, true bread IN NATURE.

source_text: Item: Sicut Johannes Baptista figuraliter fuit Elias, & non personaliter, ita panis in altari FIGURALITER est corpus Christi, & absque omni ambiguitate hæc est FIGURATA locutio, sicut illa: Johannes ipse est Elias.
english: As John the Baptist was figurally Elijah, not personally, so the altar bread is FIGURALLY Christ’s body.
Without ambiguity this is FIGURATIVE speech — like ‘John himself is Elijah.’

source_text: Et infra: Nec audiendi sunt Heretici qui sensum istum nituntur excludere, per hoc falsum: quod Evangelium nec ante, nec post, habet talem modum loquendi figurativum; Nam Lucæ 22. statim subjungitur: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Acsi diceretur: Hic panis sacramentalis inefficacem mei memoriam capi debet, cum mens Catholici non capiat, quod panis sit corpus Christi nisi intelligendo FIGURATIVE.
english: Heretics who deny any figurative Gospel speech are not to be heard — Luke 22 at once adds ‘Do this in remembrance of me.’
As if: this sacramental bread is for efficacious memory of me; the Catholic mind grasps bread as Christ’s body only by understanding FIGURATIVELY.

source_text: CONSUBSTANTIATIONEM autem hisce refutat: Sum certus, inquit, quod sententia Impanationis est impossibilis atque hæreticæ, quia sic corpus Christi nedum foret factum à Presbytero celebrante, sed & à pistore; & generaliter Sacerdos celebrans, collum & omnia membra Christi frangeret.
english: Against Consubstantiation / Impanation Wycliffe is certain: the sentence is impossible and heretical.
Otherwise Christ’s body would be made not only by the celebrating priest but by the baker — and the celebrant would break Christ’s neck and all His members.

source_text: Idem alibi, libro de Eucharistia cap. 4. Sanctus (inquit) Ambrosius non intendit dicere, quòd panis fiat identicè corpus Christi, sed quod fiat ejus FIGURA EFFICAX. Observa, FIGURAM EFFICACEM Wiclephum in Cœna statuere, quâ ratione & verba institutionis figuratè intelligenda, & præsentiam interim corporis Christi realissimam, à qua omnis Eucharistiæ efficacitas promanat, in S. Eucharistia omninò admittendam esse, contendit.
english: On the Eucharist ch. 4: Ambrose does not mean bread becomes identically Christ’s body, but His EFFICACIOUS FIGURE.
So Wycliffe holds both: Institution words figurative, and the most real presence of Christ’s body — source of all Eucharistic efficacy — fully admitted. Stop before §.XIX.

source_text: §. XIX. Waldenses in Anglia, sub Wiclephitarum nomine, Seculo XIV. celebres, excipiunt SECULO XV. WALDENSES BOHEMI, HUSSITÆ cognominati à Johanne Husso, Wiclephi Discipulo, perque Scripta Wiclephi, ab Hieronymo Pragensi, ex Anglia in Bohemiam, delata, veram sententiam adversus Papatum egregiè edocto.
english: §.XIX: the Waldenses celebrated in England under the Wycliffites’ name in Age XIV are succeeded in Age XV by the BOHEMIAN WALDENSES.
Surnamed HUSSITES from John Hus — Wycliffe’s disciple — taught the true anti-papal sentence through Wycliffe’s writings brought from England by Jerome of Prague.

source_text: Huic etsi idem evenit, quod, post centum annos, Luthero, (de quo propheticô quôdam spiritu prædixerat, ex cineribus anseris, i. e. suis, seu Hussi (isto nomine Bohemi anserem designant) olorem, seu Lutherum resurrecturum, (quem in cineres Papistæ haut redacturi essent) ut scilicet omnem Papatum, cui innutritus erat, simul & semel abjicere minus valeret, imò potiùs, uti Lutherus, initio Reformationis, in Indulgentiis solummodò abrogandis, sic hic in Communione sub Utraque introducenda ac statuminanda, omnem operam suam collocaret, Transsubstantiatione non minus atque Lutherus, missum factâ, quin cum Consubstantiatione eodem locô habitâ, uti patet ex ipsius Hussi Tractatu de Sacramento corporis & sanguinis Domini, quem scripsit in carcere Constantiensi Anno 1415. cap. 2.
english: Hus, like Luther a century later, could not cast off the whole Papacy at once — he focused labor on Communion under Both kinds, as Luther first on Indulgences.
Transubstantiation he dismissed no less than Luther, and even set with Consubstantiation (prison Tract at Constance 1415). He had foretold a swan rising from the goose’s ashes — Luther.

source_text: tamen Sectatores Hussi à regione, in qua degebant, Bohemi Fratres, ab oppido quodam, seu Castello, nomine Tabor, Taboritæ nuncupati, veritati de S. Cœna propiores accessere, agnitâ tùm tropicâ in verbis Institutionis locutione, tùm præsentia corporis Christi in Cena, sed Spirituali duntaxat, non Naturali corporalique; manducatione item ore fidei peragendâ, hincque fidelibus peculiari, nec infidelibus communi. Hæc manifesta evadunt omnia ex Confessionibus eorum variis, Seculis XIV. & XV. in publicum editis & à Balthasare Lydro Pastore Dordraceno Anno 1616. unô Volumine, duabus constante partibus, compræhensis.
english: Hus’s followers — Bohemian Brethren / Taborites — came nearer Supper truth.

They recognize tropical Institution speech and Christ’s presence in the Supper — Spiritual only, not natural/corporal — eating by faith’s mouth, for the faithful not the unbelieving (Lydius’s collected confessions, 1616).

source_text: Parte Primâ Johannes Lucawitz, Taboritarum præcipuus doctor, contra Rokenzanam & Papistas Pragenses, ita de Sacramento Corporis & Sanguinis Christi confitetur: De hoc, ait, Sacramento, istud ex fide scripturæ tenemus & corde sinceriter credimus, quod panis quem Christus in sua Cœna accipiens, suis ad manducandum dedit discipulis, & in ejus digna perceptione per Ministerium fidelium sacerdotum reliquit memoriam suæ passionis, est in natura sua verus panis, qui pronomine, Hoc, demonstratur in hac propositione sacramentali: Hoc est corpus meum, & cum hoc verum corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum & pro nobis traditum, non identicè, non de identitate materiali intelligendo, sed sacramentaliter, realiter & verè, qui propter sui habitudinem ad corpus Christi, in sibi debita habendus est reverentia, & fideles illam venerantur non ut est panis substantia, sed de quanto, ut præmittitur, est corpus Christi, cujus verum corpus in eodem esse veraciter, sacramentaliter, SPIRITUALITER, est credendum. Non autem cum omnibus proprietatibus tam essentialibus quam accidentalibus consequentibus ipsum.
english: Lucawitz (chief Taborite doctor): the Supper bread is in its nature true bread — the ‘This’ of ‘This is my body’ points to that bread.

With it is Christ’s true body from the Virgin — not material identity, but sacramentally, really, and SPIRITUALLY; reverence for the habitude to Christ’s body, not for bread’s substance as such; not with all essential/accidental properties.

source_text: Quæ verba etiam articulum primum Confessionis Taboritarum de præsentia & adoratione Christi in Sacramento, editæ anno 1432, conficiunt… Confer Resp. Taboritarum ad articulos Synodi Pragensis…: Idcirco, inquiunt, dicimus, quòd secundum Scripturæ Sacræ sententiam, sanctorum documenta doctorum, Catholicè est credendum, ore sincerissimè confitendum, totum Jesum ejusque verum corpus & sanguinem in sacramento altaris esse veraciter, sacramentaliter ac SPIRITUALITER, veri panis ac vini remanente substantiâ, non autem cum omnibus proprietatibus, tam Essentialibus, quàm accidentalibus, consequentibus idem ipsum corpus.
english: Those words also form article 1 of the 1432 Taborite Confession on presence and adoration.

Response to the Prague Synod: believe and confess the whole Jesus — true body and blood — in the altar sacrament truly, sacramentally, SPIRITUALLY, bread and wine substance remaining, without all following properties of the body in heaven.

source_text: Præterea parte 2. … Waldenses pag. 292. de Sacramento Eucharistiæ quatuor nobis divinam Scripturam credenda proponere perhibent, quorum Primum faciunt, quod Sacramentum hoc, panis & vinum sit. Secundum, quod panis ille sit verum corpus Christi, & vinum sit verus Sanguis Christi… Quibus quidem verbis Christi si quis præpostero ordine priùs velit intellectum obtrudere… ut aut nimis in altum se subvehat, hoc est, quod velit integrum Christum inibi viventem CORPORALITER seu personaliter præsentem corporibus nostris… aut è diverso minus sese in ima dejiciat … ut nullo modo Christum hic esse ferat, sed solum NUDUM & exsangue ac nihil operans in anima, SIGNUM… Tertium… Novum Testamentum… Quartum… panis ille sit participatio corporis Christi & Vinum Sanguinis ejus… Spiritualem manducandi Corporis Christi modum, excluso corporali, innumeris vicibus inculcantes…
english: Waldenses to Vladislaus (part 2): Scripture proposes four heads — (1) the Sacrament is bread and wine; (2) that bread/wine are Christ’s true body and Blood; (3) New Testament/covenant; (4) participation of body and blood.

Beware two ditches: lifting too high into CORPORAL/personal presence to our bodies, or sinking to a BARE bloodless Sign — they inculcate Spiritual eating, corporal shut out. Stop before §.XX (Lutheran comparison).

source_text: §. XX. Et hæc est causa quare Biga Clarissimorum Theologorum Lutheranorum, JOHANNES CONRADUS DANHAUERUS Argentoratensis, & ÆGIDIUS STRAUCHIUS Wittebergensis, in suis, de Waldensium Ecclesia, Dissertationibus, horum, cum sua, de S. Cœna, fide, conciliatura & Waldenses Lutheranæ fidei testes & socios ostensura,
english: §.XX: this is why two famous Lutheran theologians — DANHAUER of Strasbourg and STRAUCH of Wittenberg — write dissertations on the Waldensian Church.
They mean to reconcile the Waldenses with their own Supper faith and show them as witnesses and allies of the Lutheran faith.

source_text: (1) tamen fateri necesse habet, minus claram esse Waldensium Confessionem, quæ apud Sleidanum extet lib. 16. puta, eam in partem, claram, ut cum Lutherana videri possit eadem, quia dicunt: Esse S. Cœnam gratiarum actionem & beneficii per Christum accepti commemorationem. Imò verò Strauchius Aphorismum suum 10, capitis secundi, ita format: De Cœna Domini minùs certum est, quid omnes (Waldenses) sentiant, ac multo minus quid olim senserint: Quamvis enim Picardi orthodoxè articulum hunc exponere videantur, aliorum tamen Confessiones obscuriores sunt, quàm ut Zwinglianismum in iisdem damnari luculenter appareat.
english: (1) Yet they must admit the Waldensian Confession in Sleidanus Book 16 is less clear than a Lutheran twin — it calls the Supper thanksgiving and commemoration of the benefit received through Christ.

Strauch’s Aphorism 10: less certain what all Waldenses sense, still less what they once sensed — Picards may look orthodox, but other confessions are too obscure for Zwinglianism to appear lucidly condemned.

source_text: (2) Introductura eam Confessionis Waldensium partem, quâ Corporis Christi in Cœna præsentiam isti profitentur, à Reformatis non minùs quàm Lutheranis admissam, alteram tamen Confessionis partem, quâ præsentiæ hujus modum ubique deprædicant Spiritualem, corporali oppositum, alto silentio involvit Danhauerus §. 31. & Strauchius cit. aphorism. in ekthesei §. 1. (3) Organon manducationis corporis Christi ex mente Waldensium expositurus Strauchius, de Waldensium cum Lutheranis Consensu planè desperat, ita §. 2. scribens: Cæterùm cum in aliis Waldensium Confessionibus obscuriuscule exponatur sacramentorum doctrina, & organon participandi rei cælestis plerumque FIDES nominetur, aliorum sit de Orthodoxia Waldensium Neotericorum, & imprimis eorum qui Calvinianorum tutelam implorant, judicium &c. &c.
english: (2) Danhauer and Strauch parade the confession’s presence half (admitted by Reformed and Lutheran alike) but wrap in deep silence the half that everywhere preaches the mode as Spiritual, opposed to corporal.

(3) On the organ of eating, Strauch plainly despairs of Lutheran consensus — other confessions obscurely name FAITH as the organ of sharing the heavenly thing; let others judge neoteric Waldenses who seek Calvinist protection.

source_text: Equidem pro Consensu Waldensium Juniorum cum Lutheranis in puncto de S. Cœna, introduci posset, Articulus primus Taboritarum contra Papistas Pragenses de præsentia & adoratione Christi in Sacramento, à neutro licet Theologorum binorum, in Dissertationibus eorum notatus, quô expressè perhibent: Cum pane verè esse corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum pro nobis traditum. Item: Corpus Christi in pane esse: Quæ duæ formulæ dicendi exactè respondent tô In, Cum, & Sub Lutherano. At (1) In eodem articulo contendunt Taboritæ, pronomen, Hoc, in propositione Christi: hoc est Corpus meum, aliud nihil, quàm panem demonstrare, id quod à mente Lutheranorum modernorum omnino alienum est.
english: A Taborite article neither Danhauer nor Strauch noted could seem to serve junior-Waldenses–Lutheran consensus: ‘with the bread truly Christ’s body’ and ‘Christ’s body in the bread’ — formulas matching Lutheran In, Cum, and Sub.
But (1) in the same article the Taborites make Hoc in ‘This is my Body’ point to nothing but the bread — wholly alien to the modern Lutheran mind.

source_text: (2) Addunt, cum & in pane, esse tantum SACRAMENTALITER ET SPIRITUALITER, non autem communibus proprietatibus, tam essentialibus, quàm Accidentalibus consequentibus, quale tantùm ad dextram patris in Cœlo sit & ad quod omnis fidelis in mente debeat attendere, suspensâ consideratione circa naturam Materialis substantiæ sacramenti: Disertius adhuc idem, paulò post verba, à Danhauero, pro Waldensium cum Lutheranis consensu, in medium adducta, ita profitentes; Annon Christus ipsemet eos qui eum, post abitum illius corporalem, in terris corporaliter præsentem profitentur, dicentes, hic aut illic (in pane) est Christus, vocat Pseudoprophetas, à quibus diligenter cavendis suos præmonet. (3) Esse in pane Corpus Christi, tantum non innumeris in locis exponunt per tô esse corpus Christi in Sacramento SPIRITUALITER.
english: (2) With and in the bread the body is only SACRAMENTALLY AND SPIRITUALLY — not with heaven’s essential/accidental properties; the faithful mind attends to what is at the Father’s right, suspending material-substance fixation.

After Danhauer’s ‘consensus’ quotes they add: those who after Christ’s corporal departure say ‘here or there (in the bread) is Christ’ He Himself calls false prophets. (3) ‘Body in the bread’ they almost endlessly gloss as body in the Sacrament SPIRITUALLY.

source_text: Audiamus illos loquentes…: In Sacramentis verò est, inquiunt, Corpus Christi… atque hinc est ut in sacramentis profiteamur Christum esse non PERSONALITER aut CORPORALITER, sive SENSIBILITER nostris sensibus ac corpori, sed solum essendi MODO jam dicto SPIRITUALI… utrobique SPIRITUALITER, POTENTIA SCIL. SUA AC EFICACIA, HIC OPERANDO SALUTEM OMNI CREDENTI… Christus adsit in Sacramento NON CORPORALITER ac sensibiliter corpori nostro, sed MODO ESSENDI SUO SPIRITUALI… Nec est cur Ægidius Strauchius… dicat: Optandum esse ut haberemus antiquorum Waldensium genuinam Confessionem… Nam & hanc, ex parte saltem, habemus, istamque partem adduximus suprà §. 16., Lutheranæ Sententiæ è diametro adversam. Ut permotus videatur hôc ipsô B. Georgius Calixtus…: Waldenses, inquit, sive Picardos Bohemiæ & Moraviæ, præsentiam veri Corporis in Eucharistia, negasse notum est.
english: Hear them: in the sacraments Christ’s Body is present — not PERSONALLY, CORPORALLY, or SENSIBLY to our body, but only in the SPIRITUAL mode of being, by power and efficacy working salvation for every believer.

Strauch need not wish for an ancient Waldensian confession — we already have part of it above (§.16), diametrically against the Lutheran sentence; Calixtus notes the Bohemian/Moravian Picards denied true-Body presence in the Eucharist. Stop before §.XXI.

source_text: §. XXI. Waldensium tàm Veterum, quàm Novorum, de Sacra Cœna sententia, etsi quandoque (quod citatis retrò Theologis Lutheranis facile dabimus) obscurius proposita, SECULO XVII ad istam tamen potissimum Protestantium, i.e. Papismum oppugnantium, partem transiit, quæ REFORMATORUM nomine hodieque venit.
english: §.XXI: the Waldenses’ Supper sentence — old and new — is sometimes obscure (as the Lutheran critics said), yet in Age XVII it passed to the chief anti-papal Protestant wing.
That wing still bears the name REFORMED.

source_text: Probant id tam Confessiones horum publicæ, quam Privatorum Doctorum celebriorum Scripta, adhuc novissimè ex Harmonia Confessionum aliisque eorum Libris, collecta & recensita, tùm à Reformato Cosino, Episcopo Dunelmensi, in Historia Transsubstantiationis Papalis, cap. 2. integro, tùm à Lutherano Abbate Lutherensi, Doctore & Professore Helmstadiensi in Consideratione Controversiarum à pag. 492. ad pag. seq.
english: Proof stands in the Reformed public confessions and celebrated private doctors’ writings — freshly gathered from the Harmony of Confessions and related books.
Cosin (Durham) treats it in his History of Papal Transubstantiation ch. 2 entire; the Lutheran Helmstedt abbot in Consideration of Controversies from p. 492 on.

source_text: vindicata insuper ab horum priori §. XIII., ex Scriptis Buceri Anglicis, Zwinglii & Tigurinorum veterum sententiâ, quà modum loquendi æquè atque quà Rem & veritatem, Berengarium studiosius & ad superstitionem usque æmulantium, intereà cum ipso etiam Luthero quàm facillimè conciliandorum, quemadmodum id latius & ex professo evicimus in præfatione ad scripta Buceri Eucharistica, propediem in luci publica redonanda parag. 15.
english: Further vindication (their prior §.XIII): Bucer’s English writings and old Zwingli/Tigurine sentence — eager even to superstition after Berengar’s manner of speech and the Thing itself.
Yet they are most easily reconciled even with Luther — as Strimesius showed at large in the preface to Bucer’s Eucharistic writings (§15).

source_text: Hộc locô in superpondium doctrinæ & Fidei de præsentia corporis Christi, in S. Cœna, realissima, utut spirituali, tam Confessionibus Reformatorum publicis, quàm privatorum Doctorum Scriptis, quin in Ecclesiis nostris Germanicis, Laici cujusvis adstipulationi quotidianæ, receptæ & frequentatæ, adjicimus efficacissimas quasdam expressiones Liturgicas, tàm ante, quam post administratam apud eos in Germania S. Cœnam, prælegi solitas, ipsis quoque precibus, ad Deum hoc tempore fundendis, insertas sequentes.
english: Here, as superweight for the most real though spiritual presence of Christ’s body in the Supper, add not only public confessions and private writings,
but the German churches’ daily lay assent — and the most efficacious liturgical expressions read before and after the Supper in Germany, inserted in the prayers of the hour.

source_text: Ante Administrationem quidem precesque, quando confitentur: Das Christus selbst (verstehe vornehmlich seinem gecreuzigtem Fleisch und vergossenem Blut nach) unseren hungerigen und durstigen Seelen / zur wahren Speiß und Tranck des ewigen Lebens worden sey. i. e. Christum ipsum (puta corpore præcipuè suô crucifixô & sanguine effusô) animabus nostris esurientibus ac sitientibus, in verum cibum potumque cedere. In precibus, administrationi præmissis, quando Deo supplicant: Daß ihre mühselige und zerschlagene Herzen / mit Christi wahrem Leib und Blut / ja mit ihm / wahren GOTT und Menschen / dem wahren Himmel Brodt / durch die Krafft des Heil. Geistes / gespeiset und erquicket werden. i. e. quò animæ suæ fatigatæ ac dilaceratæ, verô Christi corpore & sanguine, quin ipso totô, DEO verô homineque, æterno illo pane cœlesti vescantur ac refocillentur.
english: Before administration they confess: Christ Himself — chiefly as crucified flesh and poured blood — has become true food and drink of eternal life to hungry, thirsty souls.
In the preceding prayers they ask that crushed hearts be fed and refreshed with Christ’s true Body and Blood — yes with Him, true God and Man, heaven’s bread — by the Holy Spirit’s power.

source_text: Denique, post preces finitas, quando Communicantes in universum omnes graviter monemur: Daß wir mit unseren Herzen nicht an dem äusserlichen Brodt und Wein hafften sollen; Sondern unsere Herzen und Glauben gründen auff das Wort der Verheissung: Und nicht zweiffeln / daß wir so warhafftig / durch die Wirckung des Heiligen Geistes / mit des HERRN Leib und Blut / an unseren Seelen, gespeiset und getränket werden / als wir das heilige Brodt und Tranck zu seiner Gedächtniß empfangen. i. e. ne cordibus nostris animisque pani & vino, externis symbolis adhærescamus, sed mentes Fidemque in Verbis Promissionis defixas habeamus, nulli dubitantes, nos non minus verè, per operationem Spiritûs S. ipsissimo Domini Salvatoris corpore & sanguine, quà animas nostras, escari potarique, quàm panem consecratum potumque in commemorationem Christi accipimus.
english: After the prayers, communicants are warned: do not cling to outward bread and wine; ground heart and faith on the Word of Promise.

Doubt not that by the Spirit’s working we are as truly fed and given drink at our souls with the Lord’s Body and Blood as we receive the holy bread and cup in His remembrance. Stop before the next § (spiritual-presence modes digression).

limits: Sampling and structural checks do not prove whole-work fidelity or completeness.
